$comment: Provenance of the vendored canonical contract and its normative test vectors.
vizra-search never edits these files; vizra-core owns them. The contract-drift
lane verifies BOTH digests, so an in-place edit here fails CI by design.
If the contract is wrong it is changed in vizra-core and re-vendored here.
$provenance_note: Provenance is recorded as the FULL refname that was resolved plus the tip it pointed
at, never a string derived from the caller's --ref argument. An earlier version wrote
args.ref.split('/')[-1], which laundered a branch named fake/main into source_ref:
'main' — the PR #1 defect (a pin on a ref that a squash-merge can delete) reintroduced
inside its own prevention. scripts/vendor-contract.py now resolves the ref to a full
refname and accepts only refs/remotes/<remote>/main, measures the checkout's remote URL
and refuses a non-canonical repository, refuses a shallow clone, and checks --commit
ancestry against the resolved ref. Each refusal has a fixture in
LIMIT: a local clone's remote URL and refs are whatever its owner set them to and the
script never fetches, so this defends against a mistake, not against someone who
controls the checkout. It does not authenticate core's bytes; the control for poisoned
normative bytes is contract-drift, where the 5 ACCEPT and 24 REJECT vectors are consumed.
authority: ADR-002 (Accepted 2026-09-20) and the Q-001 ruling: the internal contract is written in core's canonical OpenAPI and drift-checked in both repos. The vectors file declares itself normative for both repositories.

files.role: normative HMAC conformance vectors: `vectors` are ACCEPT cases, `negative_vectors` are REJECT cases, and an implementation MUST consume both halves
